eyebrow: Check it first, on any MySQL server
caption: T-SQL has no equivalent switch — bad data is always rejected there.

eyebrow: STRICT mode: warning vs. hard error
caption: Strict mode makes MySQL reject bad data instead of reshaping it.

code:
-- HARD ERROR in T-SQL, and in modern MySQL (default since 5.7)
-- Older MySQL silently picked an arbitrary CustomerName per group
SELECT CustomerId, CustomerName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerId;
caption: A real, version-dependent gotcha if you read older MySQL tutorials.

code:
-- Session only
SET SESSION sql_mode = 'STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY';

-- Permanent: edit my.cnf / my.ini, not just SQL
-- [mysqld]
-- sql_mode = "STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,NO_ZERO_DATE"
caption: Same query text, different sql_mode, different behavior — know which server you're on.
